item.title: The Weekly Juventus Digest: Como, a striker debate and the Sunday that tells us what this Juve really is
item.description: Juve thrashed Venezia 4-0 with a second-half surge and now face a defining Serie A trip to fifth-placed Como, five points ahead, as Spalletti fields striker questions.

item.title: The Weekly Inter Digest: Inter's week of extremes: a 4-4 at Bergamo, then a clean sheet against Stuttgart
item.description: Inter threw away a 4-2 lead at Atalanta despite Pio Esposito's hat-trick, then answered with a 2-0 Champions League win over Stuttgart.

item.title: The Weekly Como Digest: Eight wins in nine, and no striker needed: Como go third in Europe
item.description: Headers from Ramón and Da Cunha and a Milla curler beat Cagliari and AEK Athens, lifting Como to third in Europe before Juventus visit on Sunday.

item.title: The Weekly AC Milan Digest: Final call in Piraeus: can Amorim's Serie A machine finally travel?
item.description: Milan visit Olympiacos 28th in the Europa League and nine players short, needing a win to close the gap between their Serie A form and their European slump.

item.title: The Weekly PSG Digest: Without Doué and Kvaratskhelia, PSG test their 12-game run against Gasperini's Roma
item.description: Two ACL tears in a month have cost PSG both first-choice wingers as Luis Enrique's side take a 12-game winning run into tonight's Champions League meeting with Roma.

item.title: The Weekly Borussia Dortmund Digest: A point at the Emirates, top of the Bundesliga: Dortmund's week of statements
item.description: Dortmund drew 1-1 at Arsenal through Beier after going top of the Bundesliga at Gladbach; Leverkusen visit on Sunday with the lead on the line.

item.title: The Weekly Bayern Munich Digest: Without Kane and Olise, Bayern begin a winter of improvisation in Lille
item.description: Harry Kane's ankle surgery and Michael Olise's foot injury strip Bayern of their attack for tonight's Champions League trip to Lille and the run to Christmas.

item.title: The Weekly Real Madrid Digest: Nine straight wins, a late-goal habit and PSV at the Bernabéu
item.description: Madrid came from behind to beat Celta for a ninth straight win and now host PSV, top of the Eredivisie but 24th in the Champions League, with Vinicius back in the XI.

item.title: The Weekly Barcelona Digest: Two down in seven minutes, three goals in ten: how Barça turned Villarreal around
item.description: Barça came from 0-2 down to beat Villarreal 3-2 and stay three points clear, but go to Sabah without Lamine Yamal and may lose Fermín for two games.

item.title: The Weekly Atletico Madrid Digest: Simeone reaches 345 and Atlético find their edge again
item.description: Atlético’s 3-0 win at Getafe made Diego Simeone LaLiga’s winningest coach, but a side 23rd in the Champions League must now beat Viking.

item.title: The Weekly Arsenal Digest: Four contracts in three days: Arsenal lock down the champions
item.description: Arsenal agreed four new contracts in three days as Andrea Berta locked down the spine of the title-winning squad, with Calafiori next in line.

item.title: The Weekly Manchester United Digest: Eight minutes into the Pochettino era, United's season found a new low
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino's first game as Manchester United head coach ended 4-0 at Anfield after an eighth-minute red card, leaving United 19th with 8 points.

item.title: The Weekly Manchester City Digest: Four without a win, and De Bruyne is coming back
item.description: City drew with Fulham for a fourth league game without a win, and now host a depleted Napoli and Kevin De Bruyne before a trip to leaders Arsenal.

item.title: The Weekly Liverpool Digest: Wirtz and Ngumoha run riot as Liverpool take Pochettino's United apart
item.description: Liverpool beat ten-man Manchester United 4-0 at Anfield as Wirtz and Ngumoha ran riot, a statement win before Wednesday's Champions League trip to Club Brugge.

item.title: The Weekly Chelsea Digest: Fragile at the Bridge: Leeds rout lays bare what Alonso's Chelsea lack
item.description: Leeds won 4-1 at Stamford Bridge, exposing a fragile Chelsea side as Xabi Alonso keeps the owners' backing before Friday's trip to Nottingham Forest.

item.title: The Weekly Soccer Digest: Pochettino Walks Into The Oldest Fight In England
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino takes charge of Manchester United for the first time at Anfield on Sunday, four days into the job with his club in the relegation zone.

item.title: The Weekly Juventus Digest: Venezia at home, and no more room for drift
item.description: Juventus return from the break seventh and 11 points off the top, with Venezia at home, a long injury list easing and Conte openly talking about a comeback.

item.title: The Weekly Inter Digest: Lautaro and Thuram return as Inter restart the chase in Bergamo
item.description: Lautaro Martinez and Marcus Thuram are back in training as second-placed Inter visit Atalanta on Sunday, a point behind Lazio, with Stuttgart three days later.

item.title: The Weekly Como Digest: Douvikas alone: Como's striker crisis meets four games in 12 days
item.description: A new tibia setback for Moise Kean leaves Tasos Douvikas as the only fit Como striker for four home games in 12 days, starting with Cagliari on Saturday and AEK Athens on Tuesday.

item.title: The Weekly AC Milan Digest: Five points back, three games in nine days: Amorim's Milan restart the chase
item.description: Fourth and five points off the top, Amorim's Milan resume against Frosinone at San Siro before a pivotal Europa League trip to Olympiacos.

item.title: The Weekly PSG Digest: Eleven straight wins, and the injured stars are almost back
item.description: PSG return from the international break at Nice chasing a 12th straight win, with Dembélé, Marquinhos and Nuno Mendes close to fitness and Doué a doubt.

item.title: The Weekly Bayern Munich Digest: Kompany comes home: Bayern's coach returns for Köln, and the unbeaten interregnum ends
item.description: Vincent Kompany returns for Friday's game with Koln after his October collapse, inheriting an unbeaten Bayern side level on points with Dortmund and short of Neuer and Davies.

item.title: The Weekly Real Madrid Digest: Vinícius returns with five goals, and Mourinho has a choice to make
item.description: Vinicius returns from the break with five Brazil goals, Tchouameni is a doubt and Madrid face three home games in eight days, starting with Celta Vigo.

item.title: The Weekly Barcelona Digest: A costly break: Cubarsí a doubt as Barça face seven games in 21 days
item.description: Barça return from the international break with Cubarsí a doubt, Raphinha chastened and seven games in 21 days, starting with Villarreal at Spotify Camp Nou on Sunday.

item.title: The Weekly Atletico Madrid Digest: Atlético's November gauntlet starts at Getafe, with history in reach and bodies short
item.description: Atlético come out of the international break short of Lookman, Pubill and Cuti Romero, with Simeone one win from a La Liga record and four games in eleven days ahead.

item.title: The Weekly Arsenal Digest: Arsenal Spend the Break Locking the Doors
item.description: Declan Rice has agreed a new five-year Arsenal deal to 2031, with David Raya, Jurrien Timber and Piero Hincapie close behind, turning a quiet international break into Arsenal's biggest week of business.

item.title: The Weekly Manchester United Digest: Pochettino takes over a club in the bottom three
item.description: Manchester United sacked Michael Carrick with the team 18th and hired Mauricio Pochettino, who starts on November 18 and makes his debut at Anfield on November 22.

item.title: The Weekly Manchester City Digest: Eight days that will define Maresca's autumn
item.description: City return from the break with Fulham, Napoli and leaders Arsenal in eight days, needing to fix a leaky defence while Guéhi is a doubt and an appeal date looms.

item.title: The Weekly Liverpool Digest: Pochettino's United arrive at Anfield as Liverpool count the cost of the break
item.description: Liverpool return from the international break to face Pochettino's first Manchester United side at Anfield, with Van Dijk, Szoboszlai, Araujo and Gravenberch all fitness questions.

item.title: The Weekly Chelsea Digest: Ten games in, Alonso's Chelsea need Leeds to be a turning point
item.description: Fifth and two points off the top four, Chelsea return from the break against Leeds with João Pedro doubtful and questions to answer after the defeat at Sunderland.

item.title: The Weekly Soccer Digest: Pochettino swaps the USMNT for a United rescue mission
item.description: Manchester United sack Michael Carrick and hire USMNT coach Mauricio Pochettino, who starts on 18 November and goes to Anfield four days later.

item.title: The Weekly Juventus Digest: Six points off fourth, and a fortnight to fix it
item.description: Juventus drew 2-2 at Fiorentina to sit seventh, six points off fourth, as Spalletti faces growing scrutiny heading into the international break and a home game with Venezia.

item.title: The Weekly Inter Digest: Inter give Como the ball and take the points
item.description: Inter beat Como 2-0 with only 43 percent of the ball to go into the international break a point behind Lazio, with Sarri's injury-hit Atalanta up next.

item.title: The Weekly Como Digest: Back to earth at San Siro: what Inter exposed, and what the break must fix
item.description: Four days after a record 9-1 at Lens, Como lost 2-0 at Inter, ending a six-game winning run and dropping to fifth before the November break.

item.title: The Weekly AC Milan Digest: Amorim's split season: a Serie A contender, a Europa League emergency
item.description: Milan sit fourth on 24 points after winning at Genoa, but a 2-0 home loss to Ferencvaros leaves them 28th in the Europa League and Amorim admitting the squad is not ready.

item.title: The Weekly PSG Digest: Eleven straight wins, and PSG did it without their stars
item.description: PSG reach the international break on an 11-match winning run built without Kvaratskhelia, Dembélé and Marquinhos, and will not buy a winter replacement for the Georgian.

item.title: The Weekly Borussia Dortmund Digest: Two tight wins, 21 points and the closest title race in years
item.description: Dortmund beat Real Betis and Elversberg 2-1 to stay level with Bayern on 21 points, but fatigue and injuries to Guirassy and Chukwuemeka cloud the international break.

item.title: The Weekly Bayern Munich Digest: Kane signs on to 2029 as Bayern lead the table into a bruising break
item.description: Harry Kane extends to 2029 at a reported club-record salary while Bayern lead the Bundesliga on goal difference without Kompany, Neuer, Musiala and Saibari.

item.title: The Weekly Arsenal Digest: Five Clear, Seven Clean Sheets, One Winger Missing
item.description: Arsenal reach the last international break of the year top of the Premier League on 27 points, five clear, with the meanest defence in the division and Bukayo Saka still weeks away.

item.title: The Weekly Real Madrid Digest: Eight in a row, and Mourinho's Madrid have found a shape
item.description: Real Madrid head into the November break on an eight-game winning run, three points behind Barcelona, with Diomande's rise and Vinicius's slump the key questions.
